newsitem.title: JORDAN: Amman stock in second day drop.
newsitem.headline: Amman stock in second day drop.

text.p: Jordan's stock market fell on Tuesday for the second consecutive day after a global fund buying spree came to a halt and active selling by local portfolios dampened prices, dealers said.
The official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index dropped another 1.16 points to close at 161.11 points in substantially reduced turnover worth one million dinars ($1.4 million).

Global funds, which have fuelled a revival in bourse fortunes by aggressive buying in the last two weeks focused primarily on the cement sector and two mining stocks, have since Sunday begun avoiding large orders.
Star performer Jordan Cement, which spearheaded the rise in prices to their highest levels in two years, suffered on Tuesday from a drop in foreign inspired buying orders.
It shed 0.01 dinars to close at 4.18 dinars in substantially lower trade worth 230,379 dinars.

Brokers also detected some selling by the state investment arm, Jordan Investment Corporation (JIC), which holds extensive portfolios on two emerging fund favourites: Jordan Phosphate Mines and Arab Potash.

The two majority state-owned mining firms fell 0.02 dinars to 3.98 dinars and 0.25 dinars to 6.75 dinars respectively in barely noticeable buying. Their combined value of trade did not exceed a minimal 82,000 dinars worth of trade.
But investment analysts do not believe this is the start of a government unloading of its stock portfolio, over 40 percent of the markets capitalisation, through the stock market.
JIC, as part of a government privatisation drive, is considering selling its 33 percent stake in Jordan Cement through a GDR issue rather than a strategic industrial partner, they said.

"I strongly believe the government's intention is to go to a GDR option on two stocks, Arab Potash and Jordan Cement, before they unload their remaining holdings," said Ziad al-Basha, manager of securities in British Bank of Middle East.
The second busiest stock, Jordan National Bank, saw the heaviest local fund selling orders which sent it lower by 0.11 dinars to 2.15 dinars in 138,558 dinars worth of trade.
Overall falling shares outnumbered gainers by 36 to seven while another six traded but closed unchanged.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 best-performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance shed 0.59 percent to 81.12 points, 2.72 percent down from the start of the year.
